newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Record-breaking Aboriginal artist now down and out.
newsitem.headline: Record-breaking Aboriginal artist now down and out.

text.p: An Aboriginal painter whose work this week fetched a record price for Australian indigenous art was revealed on Wednesday to be a down-and-out welfare recipient who often sleeps in a river bed.

A 25-year-old painting by Johnny Warangkula Tjupurrula, entitled "Water Dreaming at Kalipinya", sold at auction on Monday night for A$206,000 (US$154,500) -- more than twice the previous record for a work of Aboriginal art.

But a Melbourne newspaper reported on Wednesday that, despite asking for a small portion of the proceeds, Tjupurrula would not receive a penny and would continue living on welfare in central Australia.
The artist, who is in his 70s, was one of the originators of the Papunya Tula art movement, in which Western art methods were introduced into traditional Aboriginal sand and tree-bark paintings.
In 1954, he was one of just two Aborigines chosen to meet Britain's Queen Elizabeth during a tour of Australia.
He still has a home in the town of Papunya Tula, but often visits Alice Springs, 120 km (80 miles) east, where he sleeps on a dry river bed in the city, the Melbourne Age said on Wednesday.
"Today, Tjupurrula has only two fingers on one hand and his vision is impaired," the Age said.

"He reportedly drinks heavily and often lives on handouts after his fortnightly pension has been spent. He reportedly begs for money and sells decorated spears and boomerangs to shops in Alice Springs."
The "Water Dreaming" picture was among 20 works auctioned by Sotheby's from the estate of a late Melbourne landscape artist, Tim Guthrie.

Tjupurrula had unsuccessfully asked for four percent of the proceeds from the painting's recent sale, arguing that as an Aboriginal the painting would always belong to him. He sold the painting for A$150 in 1972, the Age said.
It quoted Sotheby's director of Aboriginal and contemporary art, Tim Klingender, as saying that Tjupurrula had sold many paintings during his life, some for tens of thousands of dollars.
